transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been dealing with this constant, uncontrollable worry about almost everything in my life for the past several months. It feels like I just can't turn my brain off, and it is becoming too much to handle on my own.
Besides the constant worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or difficulty falling asleep at night?
I haven't really noticed those kinds of physical symptoms like muscle tension or trouble sleeping. My main struggle is just the constant, uncontrollable worrying going on in my head.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, or do you feel a persistent sense of sadness or worthlessness?

No, I haven't really lost interest in the things I enjoy, nor do I feel persistently sad or worthless. My main struggle is definitely more about the constant worry and anxiety rather than feeling depressed.
Do you often find that your mind wanders or that you have significant difficulty maintaining focus on tasks, even when you aren't feeling particularly anxious?

I definitely have a lot of trouble focusing on my work, but it isn't just random mind-wandering when I'm calm. Instead, these intense worries will suddenly pop into my head out of nowhere and completely disrupt whatever task I'm trying to do. It feels like I just can't keep them out.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific repetitive actions or mental rituals, such as counting or checking things, to try and neutralize these intrusive worries?

No, I don't do any repetitive physical actions or mental rituals like counting or checking things. The worries just keep spinning in my head, and I don't have any specific rituals to try and stop them.
For how many months have you been experiencing these persistent, uncontrollable worries on most days?
I've been dealing with these constant, uncontrollable worries for about nine months now. It feels like it has been happening almost every single day during this entire time.

Are these worries specifically focused on one area, like your health or social interactions, or do you find yourself worrying about a wide variety of different topics such as work, finances, and family?

It's definitely not restricted to just one area; my worry seems to spread to almost everything. I find myself constantly stressing over a wide range of everyday topics, including my performance at work, our family's finances, and the well-being of my family. It feels like my mind just jumps from one worry to the next, covering almost every aspect of my life.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry spanning multiple domains (work, finances, family) for 9 months, which is the hallmark of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. While the patient lacks some of the common somatic symptoms (muscle tension, insomnia), the persistent nature and breadth of the worry strongly support this diagnosis. Other conditions like OCD and ADHD were ruled out due to the absence of rituals and the specific nature of the distraction being worry-based rather than general inattention.
